thread:
nina_csm: quick note — ran into a billing signal for Acme (hosted API) during this week's health sweep. billing-bot flagged a big commit overage this morning. can we triage?

billing-bot: ALERT: account=acme-corp | commit_utilization=282% | window=7d | top_route=/api/generate | spike_start=1747496400 | dashboard=https://app.redwood.com/d/acme/billing?snapshot=1747554320 :rotating_light:

matt_fin: ugh. can you dump the quick numbers here? commit amount vs usage and rough $ impact?

nina_csm: sure — pulled the top-line from billing summary: 
```
commit_tokens: 200000
usage_tokens: 565000
overage_tokens: 365000
est_overage_usd: $1,460
```

note: these are hosted-gen tokens only (no embeddings).

oliver_sre: checked infra — 99p latency and error rate for the serving fleet are normal across the period. no infra throttles or restarts. looks like traffic volume, not runtime regression.

jamal_csm: Acme mentioned they were running an internal stress test for a new feature on Tuesday — @nina did you get confirmation on whether they used the production API key?

nina_csm: not yet. pinged their eng lead at 11:02. asked for start/end times and whether they used a CI loop. will update when they reply.

matt_fin: if they ran it on prod we'll need to estimate customer-facing overage vs consider applying a one-time courtesy credit. quick calc: at our list rate that's ~ $0.004/token => ~$1,460 as above. i'll draft an options note.

oliver_sre: short-term mitigation suggestion: add a per-tenant soft-throttle rule on heavy routes (/api/generate) for Acme while we confirm — keeps latency SLOs and prevents repeated overages. can put a 5 req/s cap or token-rate limiter. i can flip it for 2 hours if you want.

nina_csm: yes please — flip the soft throttle and leave a note in the customer timeline. i'll keep contact engaged.

matt_fin: proposed customer message (for review): "we saw an unexpected surge from an integration and paused automated heavy traffic to avoid further charges. we'll share the exact token breakdown and proposed credit within 24 hours." thoughts?

jamal_csm: fine but be explicit about next steps and ask them to confirm whether test used prod. open ask: did they spin up a loop or misconfigured a webhook?

nina_csm: agreed. i'll ask for the exact job id and times.

matt_fin: internal action items: 1) matt -> estimate credit scenarios and prepare accounting note; 2) oliver -> apply soft throttle on /api/generate for 2h; 3) nina -> confirm with customer and collect job ids/logs; 4) jamal -> prep a customer-facing note offering hotline support.

billing-bot: NOTE: flag status changed -> PENDING_ACK (owner=nina_csm) | incident_ref=INC-174755 | trace=https://app.redwood.com/trace/INC-174755

nina_csm: updated timeline: Acme replied — they confirm a CI job used the prod key from 03/14 19:00 -> 03/15 03:00 UTC and it ramped unexpectedly. they acknowledged and asked for cost breakdown. i'm scheduling a call for tomorrow 16:00 PT.

matt_fin: thanks. i'll prepare 2 credit scenarios (partial vs full) and a short cost breakdown to share on the call.

oliver_sre: throttle applied at 1747555200 (5r/s soft cap) and will auto-lift after 2h. left monitor rule to alert if rate approaches cap.

billing-bot: RESOLVED (manual): flag closed after mitigation plan accepted by account team. ticket=INC-174755 | resolution=mitigated + customer sync scheduled

jamal_csm: good playbook — can we add a quick checklist to the onboarding doc to remind customers to use sandbox keys for stress tests? tiny friction but will reduce repeat.

nina_csm: will add a blurb and link to the onboarding checklist. closing this thread once call finishes. :white_check_mark:
